analysis.title: From Terrific To Terrified
key_insights: Tech has moved from all-time highs to panic in less than a month. Tech implied volatility has risen the most among equity vols, and the repricing speed is described as extraordinary.

BofA says US tech is on track for its second most fragile year in over three decades, behind only 2025. Earnings reactions are getting larger while fundamentals have not deteriorated at the same pace, which TME attributes to falling conviction, AI uncertainty and reflexive positioning.
Goldman (Brad Shelofsky) says combined quarterly hyperscaler free cash flow has fallen to negative $31.4 billion. Microsoft is the only major hyperscaler still generating positive FCF.
GS (Bobby Molavi) frames hyperscalers as moving from cash-generating to cash-spending businesses. The cited problem is the cost of delivering AI demand, not the demand itself.

Taiwan's index (TWII) has fallen about 8% in the week since TME's bear Taiwan note. It broke its trend line overnight and closed well below the 100-day moving average, with little support until the 200-day moving average.
ANZ highlights the close link between Taiwan's exports and the SOX. Weak semiconductors could spill into Taiwan's real economy and make its macro strength vulnerable if the chip cycle loses momentum.

India has outperformed NDX, SOX and KOSPI over the past month. TME is not calling a new India bull market but says Indian IT has benefited from investors dumping AI-linked Asian tech, a trade it flagged in mid-October.
GS/Bloomberg data show MSCI India outperformed MSCI Asia Pacific ex-Japan by 9.7 percentage points this week, the largest weekly relative move since May 2009.

The US 10-year yield fell from about 5.3% at the top of its trend channel to about 4.9% at channel support. The 100-day moving average is slightly lower, near 4.8%. TME had flagged on October 8 that near-universal expectations of higher yields were the problem, and says anyone who played the move should take profits.
Per DB, CTAs have covered only a fraction of their bond shorts despite the Treasury rally, so the positioning unwind may be far from over.

BofA highlights IGV and SMH December call spreads as having some of the most attractive upside payout ratios among liquid ETFs. A clearing event around the midterms could trigger a sharp recovery, and defined-risk call spreads limit losses to the premium paid.

sector_views.rationale: Tech volatility has exploded, BofA flags record-level fragility, and hyperscaler free cash flow is negative. TME also notes upside convexity is becoming attractive via call spreads.
The semiconductor selloff is spreading to Taiwan, and ANZ links Taiwan's exports closely to the SOX.
Indian IT has benefited from the rotation out of AI-linked Asian technology exposure, and India has outperformed NDX, SOX and KOSPI over the past month.

earnings_insights: Goldman: combined quarterly hyperscaler free cash flow is negative $31.4 billion (a reported figure, not an estimate), with Microsoft the only major hyperscaler still positive.
BofA: earnings reactions in US tech are growing more violent even though fundamentals have not deteriorated at the same pace.

macro_indicators.reading: About 4.9% at channel support, down from about 5.3% at the top of the trend channel. The 100-day moving average is near 4.8%.
macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields have fallen sharply, but CTAs still hold a large share of their bond shorts, so further unwind is possible.
TME said then that universal expectations for higher yields were the problem. The yield has since fallen about 40bps.

trade_ideas.description: Long IGV and SMH December call spreads
trade_ideas.rationale: BofA says they offer some of the most attractive upside payout ratios among liquid ETFs, and a midterm clearing event could trigger a violent recovery.
trade_ideas.risk: Loss limited to the premium paid.

risk_factors: Spreading semiconductor selloff, including into Taiwan equities and potentially Taiwan's real economy.
Reflexive positioning and falling conviction making earnings reactions more violent.
Negative hyperscaler free cash flow as AI delivery costs rise.
Sizeable systematic bond shorts remaining, leaving the Treasury positioning unwind unfinished.
A sharp upside move in tech is possible as positioning is shaken out.
